_comment: DATA-DRIVEN so a new panel extends the tour rather than orphaning it. A tour hardcoded
in a component is one that silently stops covering the app the first time someone adds
a surface without remembering it exists.
EVERY STEP NAMES THE SELECTOR IT POINTS AT, and a browser test asserts each one resolves
against the real UI. That is what makes the tour checkable rather than a second
description of the app free to drift from it: a tour describing a feature that moved is a
doc-versus-tree defect with a spotlight on it, and the worst version of that class,
because a new user meets it first and has no way to know it is wrong.
`requiresSelection` marks a step whose target only exists once a country is selected, so
the test knows to select one before looking rather than reporting a false miss.

steps.title: The globe
steps.body: Click a country to select it. Ctrl or Cmd-click adds another and opens the compare view. Colours show how the selected country relates to each other country.

steps.title: Every number carries a badge
steps.body: OFFICIAL comes from a government or IGO source. ESTIMATE comes from a research body that publishes it as an estimate. DERIVED is computed by this app. UNVERIFIED means the provenance could not be established.

steps.title: Open the provenance inspector
steps.body: Click any value to see where it came from: the request URL, the HTTP status, when it was fetched, the raw response, the licence, and for computed values the full arithmetic.

steps.title: Why panels say "no data"
steps.body: This app never writes prose about a country. Where a source has nothing, it says so — and it distinguishes "not recorded" (we did not ask) from "none recorded" (we asked and there was nothing) from a gap that is ours rather than the country's. That is honesty, not an omission.

steps.title: Dossier tabs
steps.body: Government, Legislature, Military, Economy, News and Live TV for the selected country. Each panel states what it does not have.

steps.title: Globe layers
steps.body: Toggle event layers on the globe — earthquakes, wildfires, storms. Stale events are kept and labelled rather than hidden, because hiding them would misreport coverage.

steps.title: Every marker, as a list
steps.body: Every marker on the globe is also a keyboard-reachable entry here. Use it if a marker does not respond, or if you prefer not to aim at a sphere.

steps.title: A map of our own gaps
steps.body: Colours countries by how many of this app's panels have anything for them. It is a map of what we have connected, not of the world — and "not assessed" is shown distinctly from a score of zero.

steps.title: Score as of a past date
steps.body: Shows what this app's PRESENT evidence says about an earlier year. Not what was known then, and not a claim about what was true.

steps.title: Breaking news
steps.body: Stories ranked by a computed significance score over five normalised inputs. It ranks coverage volume, not importance — and only the coverage of the feeds this app has captured.

steps.title: Predictions, including the wrong ones
steps.body: Predictions written before this app saw live data, with what actually happened. Refutations are shown as prominently as confirmations — a watchlist that only shows its hits is an advertisement.
